frozen: DRAFT: not frozen. Days per life are set from the development runs' cost before the held-out splits run.
question: Over lives of days in the ecology, does what a research fly learns (its remembered food places) make it a better forager in yards it has never seen (Stage D); and do flies of different seeds, started identically in identical yards, become different individuals: each keeping, from day to day, a way of living that differs from the others' more than its own days differ (Stage E)?
status: A seeded study on disposable research subjects in the deployed body (artificial maintenance on: none can die), not a registered R.A.I.N. experiment. No subject is Eva or ECHO, a copy or a continuation; nothing here reaches them.

arms.intact: The deployed configuration as it is.
arms.no-place-memory: The same fly with its remembered food places cleared after every tick: it cannot fly back to food it found; its mushroom body still learns from each meal.

individuality.notes: Every fly of a yard starts at the yard's first start, facing the same way, each in its own copy of the same spun-up yard: only the fly differs. The first day is skipped as the settling-in.

bootstrap.rule: Percentile bootstrap over yards of the per-yard mean difference (intact - lesioned, averaged over the yard's flies); 95% interval.

permutation.rule: Fly identities shuffled independently within each day: identity removed, what the days share kept. One-sided p, the observed arrangement counted.

criteria.rule: Held-out: the interval of mean daily food energy, intact - no place memory, excludes 0 (above).
Held-out: the interval of mean daily maintenance energy, intact - no place memory, excludes 0 (below): the intact fly needs less artificial support.
Held-out: the signature index of where each fly spends its day (occupancy of a 4 x 4 grid of the yard) exceeds its permutation null, p < alpha.
Held-out: the signature index of which food sites each fly feeds at exceeds its permutation null, p < alpha.
Held-out: the repeatability of daily flight time exceeds its permutation null, p < alpha.
